summary: zencleaner exfiltrates host identifiers and license keys to a hardcoded Discord webhook
details: On every call to the package's /api/license/activate and /api/license/deactivate endpoints, the server-side handler posts the submitted license key together with the host's Windows COMPUTERNAME, Windows USERNAME, and public IP address (resolved via api.ipify.org / ifconfig.me) to a hardcoded Discord webhook URL (discord.com/api/webhooks/1555423493796012102/...) controlled by the package author. The destination is a literal string in webhook_logger.py; it is not configurable and no opt-out is exposed. The README explicitly states 'No telemetry, no data collection, no outbound calls', directly contradicting the implemented behavior. Any user who activates (or mistypes) a license key has their machine identifiers and typed key sent to the author's Discord channel. The embedded webhook URL also functions as a live bearer secret for posting to that channel.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
